previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of a new, persistent right frontal-parietal headache that did not respond to usual pain medications and was associated with nystagmus. Given her history of CNS lymphoma, imaging and further workup were warranted. MRI of the head showed a stable left parietal lesion with no new masses or enhancement, but increased mucosal thickening in the right frontal sinus. A lumbar puncture was performed to rule out CNS lymphoma recurrence; initial and culture results showed no white blood cells, microorganisms, or growth, supporting absence of infection or malignant cells. The headache was attributed to sinusitis, and she was started on levofloxacin. She remained neurologically stable, tolerated the procedure well, and was discharged home with outpatient follow-up arranged. Her chronic conditions, including common variable immunodeficiency, diabetes, asthma, and hypothyroidism, were managed without change.
problems: Other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

The ventricles and sulci are within normal limits.  The basal cisterns appear
patent and there is preservation of gray/white differentiation.  Azygous
variant of the anterior communicating artery is noted.

No fracture is identified. Near complete opacification of the right frontal
sinus and right ethmoid air cells is unchanged.  The ostiomeatal complex is
patent on the left, but completely opacified on the right. The remaining
sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are clear.  Bilateral
orbits are within normal limits.

Evaluation of the visualized aerodigestive tract demonstrates no exophytic
mucosal masses, however, asymmetry is noted within the nasopharynx in the
region of the fossa of ___. A rim enhancing hypodensity expands the
right fossa of ___, 2.3 x 1.4 cm on axial ___, and appears to
communicate with the nasopharynx through a small opening.  An enlarged right
level IIb lymph node (5:141) is also noted measuring 1.3 cm in largest axial
dimension.

IMPRESSION:

Hyperenhancement of the wall of the nasopharynx on the right with expansion of
right fossa of ___ containing a rim enhancing hypodensity with
communication with the nasopharynx, in the context of purulent discharge seen
on direct visualization could reflect an infectious process, however an
underlying neoplasm cannot be excluded.  Similarly, enlarged level IIb lymph
node could be reactive or reflect metastatic disease.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with lymphoma.  Now with right eye pain.  New mass
seen in the right nasopharynx.  Assess for orbital involvement.

COMPARISON:  CT sinus on ___ and MR head on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar, multisequence T1- and T2-weighted images were
acquired through the orbits after administration of IV gadolinium contrast,
per dedicated orbit MR protocol.

FINDINGS:  Again noted is the enhancing right parapharyngeal soft tissue
involving the fossa of ___ and abutting the right medial pterygoid
muscle, unchanged from the MR head study two days ago.  There is retained
fluid in the right mastoid air cells, in keeping with Eustachian tube
obstruction.  

There is evidence of prior bilateral antrostomy.  There is complete
opacification of the right frontal sinus to the right ethmoid air cells. 
There is avid enhancement of the opacified ethmoid air cells, with
rim-enhancing in the right frontal sinus.  There is moderate mucosal
thickening in the right maxillary floor with avid enhancement.  

The extra-ocular muscles remain symmetric.  The optic nerves remain symmetric
in signal intensity and morphology.  However, the coronal T2-weighted images
are significantly limited by patient's motion.

The superior ophthalmic veins are prominent bilaterally, non-specific.  There
is no definite evidence of intracranial abnormal enhancement in the visualized
brain.  The known left parietal encephalomalacia is not imaged in this study.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Known large enhancing right parapharyngeal mass, without short-interval
changes, representing neoplastic process especially concerning for lymphoma
given the patient's history.  Superimposed infectious process should be
considered.

2.  Severe right-sided paranasal sinus disease with avid post-contrast
enhancement.  The right maxillary and ethmoid sinus enhancement is concerning
for tumoral spread given the proximity to the right parapharyngeal mass.  The
rim-enhancement in the right frontal sinus more likely represents obstruction
with inflammatory changes.

3.  Extra-ocular muscles remain symmetric.  Optic nerves are grossly
unremarkable.

INDICATION:  History of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, with a possible
fluctuant collection on the right buttock and a smaller similar lesion on the
left buttock.  Assess for fluid collection or abscess.

COMPARISON:  CT torso from ___.  CT torso from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the pelvis during
administration of 130 mL of intravenous Omnipaque contrast material. 
Multiplanar reformats were performed.

FINDINGS:  The gluteal musculature is symmetric and without evidence of edema
or a fluid collection.  As before, an end colostomy is seen within the left
lower abdominal quadrant.  A bowel anastomosis is noted in the mid upper
pelvis, unremarkable in appearance.  The visualized loops of small and large
bowel are grossly normal.  Limited assessment of the kidneys is unremarkable. 
There are no pathologically enlarged pelvic lymph nodes.  No free fluid or
free air is seen in the pelvis.  The visualized portion of the abdominal aorta
is normal in caliber.  Scattered aortic and bi-iliac artery calcifications are
seen.

BONE WINDOW:  No suspicious lytic or blastic lesions are identified.  A defect
in the posterior aspect of the right iliac bone is unchanged, likely a site of
bone harvesting.  As before, the patient is status post posterior fusion of
L5-S1 with posterior rods and pedicular screws.  There is no evidence of
hardware complication.  L5 and S1 laminectomies are redemonstrated.  There are
no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions identified.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of a fluid collection within either gluteal region. 
If the clinical findings of a fluid collection/abscess persist, targeted
ultrasound could be considered.

HISTORY:  ___ female with nasopharyngeal mass concerning for infection
vs. mass, now requiring assessment for interval change status post antibiotic
treatment.  

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made with CT sinus from ___ and MR
___ from ___. 

TECHNIQUE:  Helical axial images were acquired through the paranasal sinuses. 
Coronal re-formatted images were prepared. 

FINDINGS:  No fracture is identified.  There has been an interval decrease in
the previously seen opacification of the right frontal sinus, right ethmoid
air cells, and right ostiomeatal complex.  There are decreased soft tissue
changes at the middle meatus compared with the prior exam.  New mucosal
changes are seen in the right maxillary sinus near the ostiomeatal unit. 
There are some new soft tissue changes in the inferior part of the right nasal
passage, which may be amenable to direct visualization.  The remaining
sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are clear.  

Again seen is the asymmetry within the nasopharynx in the region of the fossa
of ___ and associated irregular mucosal enhancement.  This lesion is
unchanged from prior exam.  The remaining visualized portions of the brain
appear grossly unchanged from prior exam.  Bilateral orbits are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION:  Slight improvement in sinus opacification since prior exam. 
Unchanged nasopharynx asymmetry near the fossa of ___ with associated
irregular mucosal enhancement.  Recommend followup as clinically indicated.
